svg.text: Forking CoCo for a new domain
What YOU change vs what the CODE handles. The domain.yaml file is the only seam.
What you provide
What the code handles
1. domains/<your-name>/domain.yaml
Domain vocabulary, table list, primary-key joins, ontology source (vector index), SQL guardrails, few-shot examples, evaluation prompts.
Domain loader (src/coco/domain.py)
Parses YAML, expands ${VAR} env refs, hands a typed Domain object to every component: prompts, tools, deploy, agent runtime. Validates required fields. Caches per process.
2. Your Unity Catalog tables (data.mode: existing_uc_schema)
Either point at tables already in UC, or use data.mode: synthetic with the built-in healthcare generator. Tables must match domain.yaml table list.
schema_inspector tool
Reads domain.table_names at chat time, probes each table via UC tables.get, feeds column metadata into the SQL generator prompt. No code change needed when you swap domains.
3. Knowledge documents in a UC Volume
Drop your PDFs / markdown / text into /Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<knowledge.source_volume_path>/.
Corpus chunker + AI Search hybrid index
Setup notebook reads every file in your Volume, chunks it, embeds it, and builds a hybrid (semantic + BM25) index that the ontology tool queries through domain.ontology.source.index_name.
4. Bundle deploy with --var domain=<your-name>
databricks bundle deploy -t demo --var domain=retail-marketplace databricks bundle run setup_workspace -t demo --var domain=retail-marketplace
Setup job runs in order: tables -> corpus -> index -> agent -> App
Domain spec ships as MLflow artifact to the serving container. Agent picks it up at load_context. Prompts, tools, guardrails all reflect new domain.
What you do NOT change
Agent code, ReAct loop, prompt structure, MLflow integration, AuthPolicy, App frontend, deployment automation, observability, evaluation framework.
If you find yourself editing any of those for a new domain, the domain.yaml schema is the bug, not your code. File an issue.
